title: How many restaurants, who owned them, and what they sold for
label: The numbers
lede: The company was private until 1961 and foreign-owned after 1980, so there is no run of annual filings to chart. What exists is a set of dated counts and prices from a reference history and the press of the time. Every point below is one of those; nothing is interpolated.

blocks.title: The orange roofs, counted
blocks.subtitle: Howard Johnson’s restaurants open at each date for which a sourced count exists. The dates are not evenly spaced.

points.title: rationing
points.text: Gasoline rationing closes all but 12 restaurants by the summer of 1944.[^1]

points.title: the listing
points.text: 605 restaurants at the 1961 public offering, 265 of them company-run.[^1]

points.title: the peak, and the sale
points.text: 1,040 restaurants pass to Imperial Group for $630M.[^1]

points.title: the split
points.text: Marriott takes 418 company restaurants to convert; 199 franchised ones go to Prime Motor Inns.[^2]

points.title: one left
points.text: Bangor closes on September 6, 2016. Only Lake George remains, until 2022.[^11][^14]

blocks.source: Counts for 1939–1991 from the International Directory of Company Histories[^1]; 1985 from the Los Angeles Times[^2]; 2005 from the Associated Press[^6]; 2007 from the Hartford Courant[^7]; 2016 and 2022 from Maine Public and CNN[^11][^14]. The 1985 figure (617) is derived: 350 + 68 + 199. The 1991 figure (160) is derived: about 110 franchised plus 50 owned by Marriott in mid-1991. “c. 1941” and 1954 are the source’s round figures (“about 200”, “about 400”).
blocks.note: Other sources put the peak lower: “about 850” (a chain historian quoted by the AP[^6]) and “nearly 900” (Hartford Courant[^7]). Later press usually says “about 1,000” or “more than 1,000”.[^14][^25]

blocks.title: Who ran the restaurants
blocks.subtitle: Company-operated against franchised Howard Johnson’s restaurants at four dates.
blocks.source: 1961, 1975 and 1979 from the International Directory of Company Histories[^1]; 1985 from the Los Angeles Times[^2]. Derived: 1975 franchised = 929 − 649 = 280. The 1979 split applies the source’s “75 percent company-owned” to 1,040 restaurants (780 and 260), so it is approximate.

blocks.title: What the company fetched
blocks.subtitle: Reported prices each time the business, or a piece of it, changed hands, in $ millions. Not adjusted for inflation.
blocks.source: 1979 and 1990 from the International Directory of Company Histories[^1]; 1985 from the Los Angeles Times[^2]. UPI and the Orlando Sentinel give the 1985 price as $300M, and the Sentinel gives the 1979–80 price as $650M.[^3][^4] The $235M is $97M in cash plus $138M of assumed debt.[^1] A history of Prime gives the 1990 deal as $140M for 65% of the two franchise systems.[^26]

blocks.title: For each Howard Johnson’s at the peak, McDonald’s now has about 44
blocks.equation: 45,356 ÷ 1,040 = 43.6, shown as 44 icons. McDonald’s 2025 Form 10-K[^17]; Howard Johnson’s count from the International Directory of Company Histories[^1].
blocks.source: McDonald’s Corporation Form 10-K for 2025[^17] and the International Directory of Company Histories[^1]. The comparison is across 46 years and between a worldwide and a mostly U.S. chain.
